answer: For a sonnet contest about a nebula, anchor each vote to a fresh proof of work. Validators publish an unpredictable election nonce; a voter finds a counter whose hash with that nonce and ballot falls below a fixed target. Each qualifying hash buys one voting unit and is recorded once across all keys. Splitting accounts cannot reuse a proof; more influence requires more expected hash searches for the same target. Specialized hardware can still buy influence cheaply, and computation does not establish literary merit.
